items.headline: PM Wong pledges a major review of how Singapore supports families
items.summary: In his National Day Message on Aug 8, PM Lawrence Wong announced a major review of family support spanning childcare costs and affordable infant care, and said the economy has stayed resilient amid global turbulence and AI disruption; more detail is promised at the Aug 23 National Day Rally.

items.headline: Opposition figure Lim Tean arrested in Johor Bahru after skipping his jail term
items.summary: Lawyer and Peoples Voice founder Lim Tean, 61, was arrested by Malaysian police at a Johor Bahru apartment on Aug 6 after failing to surrender at the State Courts on Aug 3 to begin a sentence of three months and one week for practising law without a valid certificate.

items.headline: Two Singaporeans charged with conspiring to help Lim Tean flee to Malaysia
items.summary: Mohammad Adam Abd Karim, 44, and Sulaiman Muhammad Firdaus, 37, were each charged on Aug 8 with conspiring to defeat the course of justice by allegedly arranging Lim Tean's illegal departure to Johor; each faces up to seven years' jail.

items.headline: Man, 22, charged over the death of a petrol-station attendant hit by a car door
items.summary: A 22-year-old man faces eight charges after allegedly reversing a deregistered car at a petrol station on Upper Changi Road North around 3:55am on Aug 6, striking a 69-year-old pump attendant with the open door; the attendant died the next day.

items.headline: Lok Sabha approves tax breaks for foreign investors in government debt
items.summary: India's lower house on Aug 7 approved, over opposition protests, a bill formalising tax exemptions for foreign institutional investors on interest and capital gains from government securities; it replaces a June ordinance that drew about $5.8 billion of inflows in June.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes a bill letting merchants charge fees on digital payments
items.summary: The lower house passed a bill allowing merchants to levy charges on online and UPI transactions, a policy shift with implications for India's largely zero-fee digital-payments regime.

items.headline: Government raises about $3.3 billion selling a 6.5% stake in LIC
items.summary: The government sold up to a 6.5% stake in state-owned LIC at 382 rupees a share, a 10% discount, raising about $3.3 billion after strong demand let it exercise an option for a further 4%; disinvestment across 10 state firms has topped 620 billion rupees this year.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The BBC and Sky News were unreachable from the routine's network today, and the permitted fallback outlets did not yield UK-domestic stories that could be verified within the 48-hour window.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign a mutual-defence pact in Mecca
items.summary: Mohammed bin Salman, President Erdogan and PM Shehbaz Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7, declaring that an armed attack on any one of the three states is an attack on all, tying nuclear-armed Pakistan and NATO's second-largest army to Saudi defence.

items.headline: A Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Najran wounds 11 amid warnings of wider attacks
items.summary: A Houthi drone-and-missile strike on Najran province on Aug 6 injured 11 civilians, including a four-year-old, according to a Saudi military spokesman, as US and Saudi intelligence warned of imminent coordinated attacks by Iran-backed groups on ports and airports.

items.headline: Update: Iran and Oman agree Strait of Hormuz shipping coordinates
items.summary: Iran and Oman said on Aug 7 they had agreed coordinates for shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, a concrete step in the US-brokered framework meant to restore the June 17 ceasefire, as President Trump predicted the war would end soon.

items.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes ignite two major Russian oil refineries
items.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said overnight strikes on Aug 8 hit the Syzran refinery in Samara and the Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar, sparking fires at both; local officials said five people were injured at Ilsky before the blaze was contained.

items.headline: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a cloud browser built for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare released Kitesurf, a Rust-based browser for AI agents that runs on its Workers platform; built in 12 weeks, it passed more than 215,000 Web Platform Tests and uses several times less CPU and memory than Chromium, the company said.

items.headline: Researchers publish the first fully AI-designed viruses in Science
items.summary: Scientists at Stanford and the Arc Institute used the Evo genome models, trained on about two million bacteriophages, to generate 302 designs; 16 worked as bacteriophages that killed E. coli, the first generative design of complete viral genomes, raising biosecurity concerns.

items.headline: Airbnb says AI now writes about 60% of its code
items.summary: Airbnb said AI tools have cut its concept-to-ship time by roughly 60% and now generate about 60% of its code, as it tests a new AI-powered search feature.

items.headline: Naive raises $28.5 million to automate setting up and running a company
items.summary: The startup Naive raised a $28.5 million Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners to automate the administrative grunt work of forming and operating a company.

items.headline: Rippling launches an AI Spend Console to track per-employee AI costs
items.summary: After spending heavily on AI internally, Rippling shipped AI Spend Console, a tool that tracks individual and team AI spending as companies adopt gateways that route prompts to cheaper models.

items.headline: Oil jumps as Iran's Strait of Hormuz draft plan revives supply fears
items.summary: Brent crude settled up about 1.25% at $83.52 and WTI rose to $78.18 on Aug 7 after Iran published a draft plan barring US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz; tracking data showed transit traffic down about 33% day-on-day.

items.headline: Atlassian soars about 30% on a cloud reacceleration and strong fiscal Q4
items.summary: Atlassian reported fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.87 a share on revenue of $1.77 billion, up 28%, with cloud revenue up 31%; upbeat guidance sent the shares up about 30% on Aug 7.

items.headline: Datadog drops about 16% as its forward guidance disappoints
items.summary: Datadog shares fell roughly 16% on Aug 7 after the cloud-monitoring firm issued weaker-than-expected revenue guidance, standing out as a software loser on a day when peers rallied on AI-driven results.

items.headline: Gold hovers near a record around $4,350 as weak jobs data fuels rate-cut bets
items.summary: Gold traded near $4,356 an ounce on Aug 7, climbing toward record territory after the surprise July payrolls decline reinforced expectations of lower US interest rates.

items.headline: Update: Bets on a September Fed rate hike collapse after the July jobs miss
items.summary: Futures cut the odds of a September Fed rate hike to about 44% from 57% and lifted the chance of a hold to roughly 60%, after employers unexpectedly shed 23,000 jobs in July; Treasury yields fell as markets unwound tightening bets.

items.headline: Swiatek fights back past Kostyuk to reach the Toronto quarter-finals
items.summary: Iga Swiatek won just one point on her own serve in the opening set but recovered to beat Marta Kostyuk 3-6, 6-1, 6-2 at the National Bank Open in Toronto, reaching her fourth WTA 1000 quarter-final of the season.

items.headline: Sabalenka downs Alexandrova to join Swiatek in the Toronto last eight
items.summary: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka beat 16th seed Ekaterina Alexandrova 6-3, 6-4 in the evening feature at Sobeys Stadium to reach the National Bank Open quarter-finals in Toronto.

items.headline: Santner's fifty fires Trent Rockets to a sixth straight Hundred win
items.summary: Trent Rockets beat MI London by six wickets at The Oval, chasing 148 with Mitchell Santner unbeaten on 52 off 23 and Tim David 32 not out; a sixth win in a row opens an eight-point lead near the top of the men's Hundred.

items.headline: Manchester Super Giants beat Southern Brave to end Brave's campaign
items.summary: Manchester Super Giants won by 10 runs at the Rose Bowl, posting 149 for 8 (Tim Seifert 50 off 30) before restricting Southern Brave to 139 for 6, a defeat that knocked Brave out of the men's Hundred.

items.headline: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause goes live as he enters the break sixth
items.summary: With Max Verstappen going into F1's summer break sixth, about 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, the performance clause letting him leave Red Bull before 2028 is now active; Red Bull have offered a new deal to remove it, but he has not signed. Next race: the Dutch GP, Aug 21-23.

items.headline: Physicists generate quantum entanglement directly from sunlight
items.summary: A University of Ottawa team, working outdoors at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, fed sunlight through a Fresnel lens and cone-shaped concentrator into a nonlinear crystal, producing entangled photon pairs at about 94% fidelity that violated Bell's inequality.

items.headline: A Cretaceous Brazilian fossil reveals surprising diversity in early snakes
items.summary: Tametara mirim, a 75-to-85-million-year-old snake and the first articulated snake fossil found in Brazil, was reconstructed by micro-CT to show a brain unlike any living or extinct snake and a head-first burrowing lifestyle.

items.headline: NASA readies a jet and 80-plus balloons to probe the corona during the Aug 12 eclipse
items.summary: For the Aug 12 total solar eclipse over Greenland, Iceland and Spain, NASA's WB-57 jet will image the corona from 50,000 feet while the Nationwide Eclipse Ballooning Project launches more than 80 balloons.

fun_fact.headline: The quietest place on Earth
fun_fact.body: The quietest place on Earth is an anechoic chamber at Microsoft's headquarters in Redmond, Washington, where the background noise measures about -20.35 decibels, far below the 0-decibel threshold of human hearing. It is so silent that visitors can hear their own heartbeat and blood flow, and the disorientation makes it hard to stay inside for long. Guinness World Records has certified it as the world's quietest room.

puzzle.title: Photo Finish
puzzle.body: Four sprinters (Ana, Ben, Cara, Dan) crossed the line in some order with no ties. Ana finished ahead of Ben; the last runner was not Cara; Dan finished immediately after Cara; Ben was neither first nor last. In what order did they finish?
puzzle.approach: Pin down the one consecutive pair first, then place the runner who can be neither first nor last.
puzzle.answer: Ana, Ben, Cara, Dan (1st to 4th). Cara-Dan must be consecutive and Ben must be 2nd or 3rd; only Cara=3rd, Dan=4th places everyone legally, forcing Ben=2nd and Ana=1st. The order is unique.

word_puzzle.title: Say It Another Way
word_puzzle.body: Each famous phrase is a perfect anagram of a second phrase that describes it: 1. ELEVEN PLUS TWO  2. THE MORSE CODE  3. A DECIMAL POINT  4. DORMITORY
word_puzzle.approach: Every letter is reused exactly once; the rearrangement is a phrase that comments on the original.
word_puzzle.answer: 1. ELEVEN PLUS TWO = TWELVE PLUS ONE (both equal 13). 2. THE MORSE CODE = HERE COME DOTS. 3. A DECIMAL POINT = I'M A DOT IN PLACE. 4. DORMITORY = DIRTY ROOM.
